artists.biography: Michael Gordon Oldfield (born 15 May 1953) is an English multi-instrumentalist musician and composer, working a style that blends progressive rock, folk, ethnic or world music, classical music, electronic music, New Age, and more recently, dance. His music is often elaborate and complex in nature. He is best known for his 1973 hit album Tubular Bells, which launched Virgin Records, and for his 1983 hit single "Moonlight Shadow". He is also well known for his hit rendition of the Christmas piece, "In Dulci Jubilo".

perplexity.description:
Released in 1975 on Virgin Records, Ommadawn is the third studio album by English multi-instrumentalist Mike Oldfield. Musically, it continues Oldfield’s signature style of extended, multi-layered compositions, blending progressive rock, folk, and ambient elements. The album is structured as a single epic piece divided into two parts, each filling one side of the original LP. It features a rich tapestry of acoustic and electric instruments, including guitars, mandolin, harp, piano, and various percussion, with a notable use of Irish folk influences and a spontaneous, chant-like vocal section at the end of Part Two. The music is characterized by its pastoral melodies, intricate arrangements, and a sense of organic progression, marking a distinct evolution from the more structured Tubular Bells and Hergest Ridge.

Ommadawn holds a pivotal place in Oldfield’s discography as his first studio album not to top the UK charts, peaking at #4, though it still achieved strong commercial success and critical acclaim. The album reflects Oldfield’s personal struggles during its creation, including anxiety and the loss of his mother, yet it stands as a testament to his resilience and creativity. Its unique blend of rock, folk, and experimental textures solidified Oldfield’s reputation as a pioneering figure in progressive and art rock, and the album remains a landmark release in the genre.
